project.name: bonobo
project.summary: Layered structural generation engine for equilibrium-informed growth, currently focused on benchmark validation for a 2D Michell-style planar problem.

current_priority.primary_goal: Validate admissible, interpretable, support-seeking growth on a canonical Michell-style planar benchmark before adding search or learned guidance.
guardrails: Preserve the graph / grammar / evaluator / experiments layer split.
Do not collapse evaluator semantics into grammar rules.
Keep ML-style arrays and descriptors as derived experiment artifacts only.
Do not expand into 3D, curved-surface, scaffold-free shell, RL, archive, or broad new typology work at this stage.

canonical_layers.role: Canonical structural state with nodes, edges, supports, loads, temp_force, metadata, and JSON roundtrip.
Proposes and applies local graph transformations through explicit rule objects.
Computes reactions, unresolved-force diagnostics, residuals, and benchmark-facing structural signals.
Defines benchmark scenarios, benchmark acceptance/ranking, descriptors, traces, summaries, and derived ML exports.

primary_benchmark.implementation_status: Approximated in the experiment layer using two fixed support nodes on the left side rather than a true continuous root boundary.

secondary_sanity_benchmark.interpretation: Previous two-support central-load planar case retained as a secondary sanity benchmark.

benchmark_mode_behavior.termination_behavior: If no admissible candidate remains, the run logs no_admissible_candidate and terminates early.

artifact_contract.current_note: experiments/last_run.json reflects the latest meaningful benchmark run; experiments/last_benchmark_report.json has been observed stale relative to the latest run directory.

current_capabilities: Draws accepted graph, explored geometry, load arrows, support symbols, and reaction arrows.
Shows chronology overlays from trace data.
Uses compas_viewer Tag labels instead of point-name fallback when available.
Draws a bounding rectangle derived from support/load geometry rather than filling the face.
viewer_state.interpretation_rule: Viewer styling and color are interpretive only; engine truth lives in the graph state, evaluator outputs, and exported artifacts.

diagnosis: This is a clean benchmark failure rather than noisy overgrowth.
The first accepted move is extend_node_rule.
The split candidate is rejected immediately for outside_bounds in the cantilever configuration.
The run then terminates with no_admissible_candidate.
Residual remains flat at 10.0 and no reactions are engaged.
The current issue is primarily benchmark-geometry versus available-rule compatibility, not a viewer problem.

seed_vs_generated_edges.note: The experiment builder currently seeds a support-to-load fan by explicitly connecting each support node to the load node before the grammar loop begins.

semantic_snapshot.temp_force: Currently an unresolved nodal imbalance signal used in growth and debug workflows.
semantic_snapshot.reactions: Evaluator-derived constrained components absorbed from temp_force at restrained DOF.
semantic_snapshot.member_force_storage: Explicit canonical member axial force/sign storage is not implemented.
semantic_snapshot.structural_progress_v1: Minimal benchmark-level notion based on residual improvement, support/root approach or connectivity improvement, and/or reduced temp_force burden while remaining geometrically admissible.

covered_areas: LOA, split-node, triangle, and temp-force closure behavior
tests.known_special_case: test_handshake.py depends on local MCP/server availability and is not a pure unit test.

known_gaps_and_uncertainties: The cantilever root is still approximated with discrete fixed nodes rather than a true support boundary.
The benchmark seed currently includes two support-to-load bars, which biases the run toward an already-connected initial fan.
Residual closure and reaction engagement are not yet achieved on the primary benchmark.
Viewer member colors, including green members, remain interpretive only.
At least one benchmark-facing doc still appears partially aligned to the older two-support framing and should be checked before treating all docs as fully synchronized.
